```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# YOUR OWN TABLE STYLES, PAGE 2 (S422 review; was Publication tables page 6;
# split from "Where your styles live" by Jeff, S422). A prose page: a line for
# the .Rprofile and some habits, so no numbered blocks, no Console panes and no
# follow-along script. The code is in plain fences, never run: the line jstats
# shows sets a folder in the render machine's own Documents folder.
#
# THE LINE (S427; built in v0.9.287, the (S427) item, Jeff's "Option 2"). The
# reader runs joptions(style.dir = NULL), then jstyle(), whose list ends, with
# no style folder set, on the line that sets one in Documents by its full path
# (the (S423) path item, v0.9.284; Jeff: "Some of my students, even at the
# masters level, have a difficult time with the ~ and the concept of a working
# directory"). No spare copy is saved (Jeff, S427: "3. okay"). The end of the
# list is QUOTED from a run at render (chunk "unset-lines"), the Documents
# folder shown as <your Documents folder>; a real path left in it halts the
# render.
#
# The finding-the-folder step names no web page (Jeff, S422: "point them to
# on-line information about this (easily found with a search - I don't want to
# worry about webpage links becoming outdated)").
#
# S428: the S427 wording pass (Fable 5.2, okayed by Jeff), adapted to the
# jstyle() route above.
#
# jstats is loaded quietly for the quotation and the prose gates; every call
# that reads or writes the jstats folder does so in a temporary one
# (R_USER_DATA_DIR, which tools::R_user_dir() reads at each call).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
options(width = 80)   # match a default 80-column console, as the quotation wraps
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(jstats))
.ks_msgs <- function(expr) {      # what a call prints, both streams, in order
  out <- character(0)
  o <- withCallingHandlers(utils::capture.output(expr),
                           message = function(c) { out <<- c(out, conditionMessage(c))
                                                   invokeRestart("muffleMessage") })
  c(o, unlist(strsplit(out, "\n", fixed = TRUE)))
}
# The Documents folder, worked out as jstats works it out: R's home folder is
# the Documents folder on Windows; on a Mac or Linux the home holds Documents.
.ks_home <- sub("/+$", "", gsub("\\", "/", path.expand("~"), fixed = TRUE))
.ks_docs <- if (identical(tolower(basename(.ks_home)), "documents")) .ks_home else
  file.path(.ks_home, "Documents")
```

## Keeping your styles

**Your own table styles &middot; Page 2**\
*The page before this one is
[1. Making your own style](tables-own-style.qmd).*

Page 1 kept its style in a folder named `Styles` inside the project. That suits
a style that belongs to one project, such as one journal's style for one paper,
but the folder is deleted when the project is: copy such a style somewhere else
before you delete the project. This page shows where to keep the styles you mean
to keep, so that every project can use them. There's no script to build here:
just a line for your project's `.Rprofile`, and a few habits.

## One folder for every project

- **Choose a folder you can see, and that is backed up.** jstats suggests one:
  a folder named `Styles` in your Documents folder.
- **Get the line that sets it.** The line is `joptions(style.dir = "...")`, with
  the folder's full path between the quotes. You don't have to type the path.
  With no style folder set, `jstyle()` ends its list of styles with the line,
  made for your computer. To see it now, run these two lines in the Console:

  ```r
  joptions(style.dir = NULL)   # no style folder, as in a new session
  jstyle()                     # lists your styles, and ends on the line
  ```

  `jstyle()` lists the styles it can find and the folders it looks in. When
  this page was made, its list ended on these lines:

  ```{r}
  #| label: unset-lines
  #| echo: false
  #| results: asis
  # The end of jstyle()'s list with no style folder set, run here and QUOTED, the
  # Documents folder shown as <your Documents folder>. Under a temporary jstats
  # folder, so the render machine's own styles are never read; nothing is
  # written.
  .ks_old_ud <- Sys.getenv("R_USER_DATA_DIR", unset = NA)
  Sys.setenv(R_USER_DATA_DIR = tempfile("ks-ud-"))
  invisible(utils::capture.output(joptions(style.dir = NULL)))
  .ks_raw <- gsub("\033\\[[0-9;]*m", "", .ks_msgs(jstyle()))   # a quotation: no color codes
  if (is.na(.ks_old_ud)) Sys.unsetenv("R_USER_DATA_DIR") else
    Sys.setenv(R_USER_DATA_DIR = .ks_old_ud)
  while (length(.ks_raw) && !nzchar(trimws(.ks_raw[length(.ks_raw)])))
    .ks_raw <- .ks_raw[-length(.ks_raw)]
  .ks_i <- grep("^No style folder is set", .ks_raw)
  if (length(.ks_i) != 1L)
    stop("unset-lines: jstyle()'s list did not end on the style-folder lines:\n",
         paste(.ks_raw, collapse = "\n"))
  .ks_end <- .ks_raw[.ks_i:length(.ks_raw)]
  .ks_line_real <- .ks_end[length(.ks_end)]
  .ks_txt <- gsub(.ks_docs, "<your Documents folder>", .ks_end, fixed = TRUE)
  if (any(grepl("(?<![A-Za-z])[A-Za-z]:[\\\\/]|/home/|/Users/|/root/|/tmp/", .ks_txt, perl = TRUE)))
    stop("unset-lines: a real path survived the placeholder:\n", paste(.ks_txt, collapse = "\n"))
  cat("```text\n", paste(.ks_txt, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
  ```

  In your Console, the last line holds the full path of your own Documents
  folder, so it works exactly as it appears there. Copy that line from your
  Console, not from this page.
- **Set it for every session.** The `style.dir` setting lasts until R
  restarts, so paste the line you copied into your project's `.Rprofile`, the
  file [Loading jstats automatically](loading-jstats-automatically.qmd) sets
  up, below its `library(jstats)` line:

  ```r
  # Explained on the Keeping your styles page
  joptions(style.dir = "<your Documents folder>/Styles")
  ```

  An `.Rprofile` belongs to one project, so add the line in each project where
  you make tables. Every project then finds the same styles. jstats creates the
  folder the first time the line runs, if it isn't there.
- **Move a style in.** A style made in a project's own `Styles` folder, as on
  page 1, can be copied into this folder like any file. With the line above in
  place, jstats looks in this folder first, so the copy here is the one it uses.

## Keep copies

A style file is a small text file. Keep a copy of any style you would hate to
lose, and of the version before a big change.

## If no style folder is set

With no style folder set, `jstyle()` with `save.as =` saves a copy in your
*jstats folder*, a folder jstats keeps for you, and shows the copy's full path,
followed by a note with the folder's own path and the line that sets a style
folder in your Documents folder. The jstats folder is easy to lose track of: it
is hidden in File Explorer on Windows (it sits under AppData) and in Finder on
a Mac (under Library).

To open it anyway, copy the folder's path from the note (`jstyle()` with
nothing in the parentheses shows it too, at the end of its list of folders) and
paste it into the address bar of File Explorer on Windows, or into Finder's
Go > Go to Folder on a Mac. To make hidden folders show all the time, search
the web for "show hidden files" and your version of Windows, or for "show
Library folder" on a Mac.

Setting a style folder of your own, as above, keeps your styles where you can
see them. Pages 3 to 5 show three ways to change a copy of a style: pick one.
Page 3, [Changing a style by hand](tables-by-hand.qmd), is the first.

```{r}
#| label: prose-gates
#| include: false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PROSE GATES -- hidden. Each stopifnot() below is one statement the prose
# makes about what the package does; a false one HALTS the render. Every file
# written goes into a temporary folder.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.msgs <- function(expr) paste(.ks_msgs(expr), collapse = "\n")
.td <- tempfile("ks-"); dir.create(.td)
.old_ud <- Sys.getenv("R_USER_DATA_DIR", unset = NA)
Sys.setenv(R_USER_DATA_DIR = file.path(.td, "userdata"))
.jf <- tools::R_user_dir("jstats")
dir.create(.jf, recursive = TRUE)
.np <- function(p) normalizePath(p, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
stopifnot(startsWith(.np(.jf), .np(.td)))   # the temporary one, never the real one
# a path as R hands it over can differ from its normalized form (Windows'
# short names, a linked temporary folder): accept either form in the text
.has_path <- function(text, path) {
  text <- gsub("\\\\", "/", text)
  any(vapply(unique(c(gsub("\\\\", "/", path), .np(path))),
             function(f) grepl(f, text, fixed = TRUE), logical(1)))
}
# the quoted lines: the line jstyle() ends on sets Documents/Styles, by
# its full path, and runs as printed (two spaces in, the path whole)
.line_want <- paste0('  joptions(style.dir = "', .ks_docs, '/Styles")')

# joptions() creates a style folder that is not there (a full path here,
# standing in for the line's Documents folder, which is the render machine's)
.newdir <- file.path(.td, "Styles")
.m_new <- .msgs(joptions(style.dir = .newdir))
.made <- dir.exists(.newdir)
# the style folder comes first: a style of the same name in the jstats folder
# is not the one used
invisible(utils::capture.output(jstyle("report", save.as = file.path(.newdir, "same"))))
.alt <- readLines(file.path(.newdir, "same.jstyle"), encoding = "UTF-8")
.alt[which(.alt == "font = Arial")[1]] <- "font = Courier New"
writeLines(.alt, file.path(.jf, "same.jstyle"), useBytes = TRUE)
.font_first <- grep("^font ", utils::capture.output(jstyle("same")), value = TRUE)[1]
# with no style folder set: save.as writes into the jstats folder and shows the
# copy's path, then a note with the folder's own path and the line; jstyle()
# lists the jstats folder last among its folders
invisible(utils::capture.output(joptions(style.dir = NULL)))
.m_save <- .ks_msgs(jstyle("report", save.as = "kept"))
.saved <- file.exists(file.path(.jf, "kept.jstyle"))
.m_save_t <- paste(.m_save, collapse = "\n")
.lst <- .ks_msgs(jstyle())
.folder_lines <- grep("\\((the style folder|the working directory|your jstats folder)", .lst, value = TRUE)
.last_folder <- .folder_lines[length(.folder_lines)]

if (is.na(.old_ud)) Sys.unsetenv("R_USER_DATA_DIR") else Sys.setenv(R_USER_DATA_DIR = .old_ud)
stopifnot(
  # the quotation: three lines and the line, which sets Documents/Styles
  length(.ks_end) == 4L, identical(.ks_line_real, .line_want),
  grepl("To keep them in your Documents folder instead, run:", .ks_end[3], fixed = TRUE),
  # the line's folder is created the first time it runs
  grepl("Created the style folder", .m_new, fixed = TRUE), .made,
  grepl("Arial$", .font_first),
  # no style folder: the copy's full path, then the note's folder path and line
  .saved, grepl("Style written to", .m_save_t, fixed = TRUE),
  .has_path(.m_save_t, file.path(.jf, "kept.jstyle")),
  any(vapply(.m_save, function(l) .has_path(trimws(l), .jf) && !grepl("kept", l), logical(1))),
  grepl("is hidden in File Explorer on Windows and in Finder on a Mac",
        gsub("\\s+", " ", .m_save_t), fixed = TRUE),   # the note is width-wrapped
  identical(.m_save[length(.m_save)], .line_want),
  # jstyle() shows the jstats folder at the end of its list of folders
  grepl("(your jstats folder", .last_folder, fixed = TRUE),
  .has_path(.last_folder, .jf)
)
unlink(.td, recursive = TRUE)
```
